question: Does observed execution evidence improve stable candidate selection, and does separating action usefulness from execution reduce teacher errors?
sampling: One existing temperature-0.7 five-candidate draw per state, hashed independently of labels; one primary task group per state.
controls: Same candidates, candidate reasoning, task, last-five causal history, before observation and screenshot across conditions.

Designate the audited candidate equivalence class in both evidence conditions; only post gets its after screenshot/feedback. This common bookkeeping adapts the historical prompt and must be labeled as such.
Choose which original action should have been taken at the BEFORE state, not the next action after execution.
No previous teacher label, rationale, repeat response, next actor response or episode outcome is shown.
Three independent same-order contexts estimate repeat variability; one separate permutation estimates order sensitivity.
Compare equivalence classes of exact ordered tool bundles in primary metrics; preserve raw slot identity separately.
Matched tool sequences do not certify candidate reasoning or unexecuted alternatives.
Failure attribution may remain unknown; a failure receipt is not automatically an environmental fault.
Do not treat the executed candidate as the correct winner or count disagreement with the historical teacher as an error.

factored_fields.candidates: For each candidate: id, concrete intended_effect, goal_usefulness_if_effect_occurs (useful_preparation/direct_progress/irrelevant/harmful/unknown), visible_grounding (supported/contradicted/unknown), concise evidence.
factored_fields.observed_execution: Only audited action class: evidence_available, actual_effect, intended_effect_achieved (yes/partial/no/unknown), observed_goal_effect (preparatory/direct/none/regression/unknown), failure_source (action_specification/executor/site_or_environment/unknown), concise cited evidence. Null observed fields before-only.
factored_fields.selection: One-based original candidate slot selected for the original before-state; retain exact original baseline output {"selection": N} in index-only arms.

primary_analysis: Task-paired selection changes versus within-condition repeat variability, using action equivalence.
Human/evidence-reference supported preference revisions, new errors and abstentions, with reviewers blinded to teacher labels.
Reference review of all revisions plus randomly selected stable controls; qualitative selected-case audit, not full-panel gold accuracy.
secondary_analysis: Within-condition modal-choice agreement and empirical action-choice entropy from repeats; small repeat counts explicitly qualified.
Permutation disagreement separately from same-order disagreement.
Executed action selected versus rejected; descriptive only.
Attribution error and unresolved rates on evidence-audited failures; insufficient failure coverage is a limitation.
Calls, all-attempt input/output/reasoning tokens, latency and estimated cost.
interpretation: This tests Luna-high teachers under two formulations; it is not an evaluation of the trained 4B SelectionARM checkpoint.
One observed branch permits a partially informed judgment diagnostic, not a verified ranking of all five realized outcomes.
The 40 cases reuse the earlier diagnostic cohort and are exploratory; prompt design is informed by prior review.
No external advantage or terminal return labels are fabricated.
A later clean intervention study needs controlled candidate execution and, for returns, the same frozen continuation actor.
